pr_title: Change Dyson PureCoolLink fan speeds to adhere the standard
pr_body:
<!--

## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->
The speed of the Dyson Pure Cool Link fan is now one of "low", "medium", and "high" instead of the original "auto" and integer 1 to 10. In order to set the fan speed more precisely and switch auto mode, users should use the services `dyson.set_speed` and `dyson.set_auto_mode`.


## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
The speeds of `DysonPureCoolLinkEntity` are changed to adhere [the standard](https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/core/entity/fan/#properties). `DysonPureCoolLinkEntity` now supports custom service `dyson.set_speed`. Similar code of `DysonPureCoolEntity` and `DysonPureCoolLinkEntity` is moved to the base class `DysonFanEntity`.

issue_context.title: Dyson dyson.set_speed service call not working
issue_context.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST:
  - If you need additional help with this template, please refer to https://www.home-assistant.io/help/reporting_issues/
  - Make sure you are running the latest version of Home Assistant before reporting an issue: https://github.com/home-assistant/core/releases
  - Do not report issues for integrations if you are using custom components or integrations.
  - Provide as many details as possible. Paste logs, configuration samples and code into the backticks.
  DO NOT DELETE ANY TEXT from this template! Otherwise, your issue may be closed without comment.
-->
## The problem
<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened.
-->
I have recently setup my 2 dyson Pure Cool (one Pure Hot and cool DP04) fans on homeassistant and am trying to automate operating the fans via the lovelace UI / Automation. 
The issue I am facing is that the **dyson.set_speed** service call works fine when invoked from the Developer Tools 
but calling the same service with the same parameters via an automation fails every time with the below shared error message.



## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Configuration -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant Core release with the issue: 0.118.2
- Operating environment (OS/Container/Supervised/Core): Dockerised version of HA no Pi
- Integration causing this issue: Dyson
- Link to integration documentation on our website: 

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->
Action code in automation script which is failing
```yaml
entity_id: fan.living_room
service: dyson.set_speed
data:
  dyson_speed: 2

```
automation code working in Developer Tools Service call 
```
entity_id: fan.living_room
dyson_speed: 2
```

and if i modify the automation to the below fan.set_speed service call, that also works fine
```
entity_id: fan.living_room
service: fan.set_speed
data:
  speed: low
```
## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

```txt
Error executing script. Invalid data for call_service at pos 1: value should be a string for dictionary value @ data['entity_id'

voluptuous.error.MultipleInvalid: value should be a string for dictionary value @ data['entity_id']
```

## Additional information
comments:
Hey there @etheralm, mind taking a look at this issue as its been labeled with an integration (`dyson`) you are listed as a [codeowner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L120) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

Another user has posted the workaround on structuring the YAML a certain way to get it working on the forums.

I can confirm the same works for me.
https://community.home-assistant.io/t/dyson-automation-dyson-set-speed/234160


```
service: dyson.set_speed
data:
  dyson_speed: 3
  entity_id: fan.living_room
```

@nabeelmoeen I think this is because the custom services in `dyson` integration are not entity services. They are just regular custom services so `entity_id` is handled by the integration itself instead of by HA. Therefore, it should be passed as a `data` field. I'm planning to switch all `dyson` services to entity services and that should fix this problem.

review_comments: We don't include items at all if the value is `None`.
Now none of them will be `None`.
